label: original-phase bigrams of tokens from {2,n,l,y,1,k} (strongest on 2)
explanation: Low end of candidate unit 76. About 89% of activation mass falls in the original (input) phase. It never fires at t=0 and rarely fires in the copy phase. It is driven by the input token: 2 has a 9.7x lift and carries 40% of the mass, followed by n (3.8x) and then l, y, 1, k. The preceding token is drawn from a similar set (2, n, 1, y, k, c, q, w). Rates are highest at t=1-2 and at the last original positions of long sequences (orig_idx 8 has an 11x lift). Sequences containing more digits fire more often. The largest activations come from input 2 at the final original step, just before <DEL>, and the unit often stays weakly active on <DEL> right after. Input 2 preceded by a token from that set gives precision 0.51 but only 22% recall. The bigram predicate catches about 60% of the mass at precision about 0.2, so the unit seems to read a distributed hidden-state direction that token identity only partly captures. It does not fire on most letters (a, f, i, p, s, u, v) or on 0/3 as inputs.
